class.name: HEGoCopiaOutput
class.brief_description: Writes a cook's points into a Copia store, on every cook of any HEGo node whose output carries them: the panel's Recook, a Session Sync update and a batch cook() all do the same.
class.description:
HEGo finds this handler because it extends [HEGoOutputHandler]; neither HEGo nor Copia names the other. It acts on points with a [code]hegocopia_object[/code] or a [code]hegocopia_clear[/code] point attribute (the table is in docs/copia/houdini.md):
[codeblock]
hegocopia_object string path of a CopiaObject (or a Mesh); non-empty = an instance P, orient or N + up, scale, pscale the transform Cd, hegocopia_custom (+ hegocopia_custom_w) optional colour and custom data hegocopia_keep float optional density priority 0..1 hegocopia_set string set to write into; blank = default hegocopia_store string node path of the CopiaStore3D from the scene root; blank = the only one hegocopia_clear int 1 = a clear point: empties set hegocopia_set in cell hegocopia_cell hegocopia_cell string "cx_cz", on clear points only [/codeblock]
Within one cook, clears are applied first and instances added after, per store. Nothing is cleared implicitly. One cook may write several sets and several stores.
Options, from the host's metadata [code]hegocopia[/code] and the cook state key [code]hegocopia_options[/code] (a cook extension's cook_prepare can set it), the later one winning per key: [code]extra_attributes[/code] ([PackedStringArray]), point attributes that are loaded too and stored as pass-through columns.
The result is left in the cook state under [code]hegocopia[/code]: [code]{stores: {path: result}, errors, warnings, point_count, clear_count, skipped_count}[/code] where each result is what [method write_attributes] returns.

method.name: write_routes
method.description: What [method handle] does with a cook's points once they are read: [param routes] maps each [code]hegocopia_store[/code] value to the attributes of the points that carry it (as [method write_attributes] takes them), and [param options] are the cook's options ([method options_of]). Store paths are resolved first and the points of every path that names the same store are written in one call, so a blank path and the store's own path (the spawned points and the clear points of the documented pattern) clear before they spawn. Returns the report the handler leaves in the cook state: [code]{stores: {path: result}, errors, warnings, point_count, clear_count, skipped_count}[/code].

method.name: split_routes
method.description: Splits the columns of a cook's points ([code]{name: one value per point}[/code]) into the routes [method write_routes] takes, by [code]hegocopia_store[/code]: points without a store and points with a blank one both go to the route [code]""[/code] (the only store). The split is native and linear; when every point names the same store (the usual case) the columns are passed on without a copy.

method.name: options_of
method.description: The options of a cook: the host's metadata, then [param cook_state]'s options on top.

method.name: merge_points
method.description: Appends the points of [param more] to [param into], attribute by attribute. A column only one side has is padded with [code]null[/code] (a point without a value), so the rows stay aligned; padded columns become plain Arrays.

method.name: write_attributes
method.description:
Writes the points in [param attributes] into [param store]: [code]{name: one value per point}[/code] as HEGo delivers them (plain Arrays, [code]null[/code] where a point has no value; packed arrays work too), under the [code]hegocopia_[/code] names above.
Clear points are applied first, then the instances added. [param options]: [code]extra[/code] ([PackedStringArray]), the names of attributes stored as pass-through columns. This is also the entry point for a cook extension that reads its points itself.
Returns [code]{ok, errors, point_count, clear_count, skipped_count, write}[/code]. [code]ok[/code] says the store took what there was to write (nothing to write is ok); [code]errors[/code] also lists what the conversion skipped or ignored, so it can be non-empty when ok. [code]write[/code] is [method CopiaStore3D.write]'s result, empty when nothing was written.

method.name: find_store
method.description: The store [param path] names, or the only store when it is blank: see [method resolve_store].

method.name: resolve_store
method.description:
Like [method find_store], with the reason when there is none: returns [code]{store, path, error}[/code], where [code]path[/code] is the store's node path from the scene root ([method scene_root]).
A non-blank [param path] is the node path from the scene root (also tried as an absolute path). A blank one means the only [code]CopiaStore3D[/code] of the scene: none, or several, is an error.

method.name: scene_root
method.description: The root node store paths are relative to: the owner of [param host] (the scene root of the scene it is saved in, which is the current scene at run time), else the edited or current scene when it holds the host, else the topmost ancestor below the window.

method.name: is_store
method.description: Whether [param node] is a [code]CopiaStore3D[/code]: its script, or one it extends, is the store's. The script is checked, not a class name the class cache may not know.

method.name: native_static
method.description: Calls a static method of a Copia native class, loading the extension if it is not yet.

constants.constant: Metadata key of the host that holds the options.
